items.t: BofA adds TSLA, AVGO, IBM, others to its Global Defenders list
sum: Bank of America this week added mega-cap names including Tesla TSLA, Broadcom AVGO, and IBM IBM to its quantitative Global Defenders list, updating its screen of richly priced equities that have lagged the market.

The screen identifies the 30 highest price-to-earnings stocks displaying below-average earnings momentum and price momentum, balanced across sectors and global regions. Global Defenders surged 4.0% in October, capitalized on a worldwide rotation where weak-momentum and value shares rebounded while high-flying momentum leaders retreated.

That gain allowed the cohort to beat the benchmark MSCI AC World Index (-1.7%) and outpace the Global Contenders strategy (-3.2%) by 7.2 percentage points, narrowing the Contenders' 12-month performance lead to 8.4%.
Among the other new entrants to the Global Defenders roster include Motorola MSI in the U.S., alongside Australia's Westpac WEBNF, China's Xpeng XPEV, and Norway's DNB Bank DNBBY.

items.t: Mideast Stocks: Gulf bourses advance as investors weigh US midterms and Iran standoff
sum: Gulf bourses advanced in early trade on Wednesday as investors weighed the fallout from the US midterms and waited to see how Washington would respond in its war with Iran.
Democrats seized the Senate and the House, dealing a setback to President Donald Trump. Their wins in South Carolina, Texas and Ohio broke through long-held Republican territory.
Saudi Arabia's benchmark index gained 1.7%, lifted by a 6.7% jump in Saudi Arabian Mining Company and a 1.4% rise in Al Rajhi Bank.

The US carried out "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm island targeting surface-to-air missiles used against US assets, a US official said on Tuesday. Another official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations.
In Qatar, the index leapt 2.3%, with almost all its constituents in positive territory including Qatar Islamic Bank , which was up 3.3%.
Doha announced on Tuesday that Washington and Tehran remain dedicated to mediation and are examining proposals meant to close the distance between them.
Qatari officials also reported recent progress in discussions with each side, and efforts to shrink the differences between them are still underway.

items.t: Mideast Stocks: Gulf bourses mixed as Iran-Saudi talks offset fears over US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
sum: Major Gulf bourses were mixed in early trade on Tuesday, as Iran's statement that talks with Saudi Arabia were continuing was offset by escalation fears in the eight-month conflict after the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

A US official said on Monday that the strikes, earlier reported by the Wall Street Journal, appeared limited and did not mark a resumption of major combat operations. The official spoke on the condition of anonymity.

Saudi Arabia's benchmark index slipped 0.2% in choppy trade, weighed down by a 0.4% fall in Al Rajhi Bank . Oil giant Saudi Aramco eased 0.2%, even though it reported a steep rise in third-quarter profit.

Aramco said on Tuesday that its net profit rose 34.5% despite attacks targeting the company. The increase came mainly from higher revenue and its exit from a joint venture. The US-Iran war has cut Aramco's output, but higher oil prices have offset the lower volumes.
Alongside the results, the company declared a base dividend of $21.9 billion.

With the conflict disrupting operations, Aramco is also looking at ways to protect its exports. CEO Amin Nasser told Reuters in a statement that the company is exploring additional export routes and overseas capacity, including a possible expansion of its East-West pipeline.
On the other hand, Al Majed for Oud Co soared 8.6%, a day after reporting 50% jump in third-quarter profit.

items.t: Alinma Bank stock: ANB Capital flags Q3 profit miss versus forecast
sum: Alinma Bank's third-quarter earnings remain under scrutiny after ANB Capital said net profit of SAR 1.58 billion came in 6.3% below its forecast. The assessment was reported in a November 1, 2026 note by Argaam.

The result places credit costs and the quality of income at the center of the investment case. A weaker-than-forecast quarterly outcome can raise the importance of provisioning trends, financing growth and fee income when investors assess the bank's next reporting period.

ANB Capital's assessment follows Alinma Bank's third-quarter reporting for 2026. The analyst view points to a gap between the reported quarterly profit and expectations, while leaving the broader earnings outlook dependent on how financing income develops alongside credit charges.
Alinma Bank stock traded at 21.59 Saudi riyals on the Saudi Exchange at 1:19:22 p.m. CET on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

Alinma Bank provides Shariah-compliant retail and corporate banking, asset management and brokerage services, with its main operations in Saudi Arabia. The bank is headquartered in Riyadh and serves the Kingdom's financial market. It competes with Al Rajhi Bank, Saudi National Bank and Bank Albilad; Alinma is positioned as a Saudi-focused Islamic lender with a broad banking and investment-services offering.
